images.filename: Former Acme Supermarket, South Main Street, Canandaigua, New York - 20210522.jpg
images.caption: The former Acme Supermarket at 212 South Main Street in Canandaigua, New York, as seen on a balmy April 2021 evening. Although it's located with in the NRHP-listed Canandaigua Historic District, the building was deemed not to be a contributing property - perhaps because of the nonconforming alterations to the façade that were present at the time of the nomination in 1984 but have since been removed by new owner Andrew Guffey with an eye to the building's history. Here we see a design that's admittedly fairly utilitarian, but boasts strong hints of the Streamline Moderne style that was all the rage at the time of its construction: the low-slung massing, horizontal orientation, the glossy finish to the exterior and the chrome accents around the windows are all trademark. Most surprising of all, especially given its level of preservation, is that the sign is original; it was perfectly preserved underneath the modern siding that was removed in 2016. This speaks to the durability of the porcelain enamel with which the sign was made, following the style of the time. Parent company American Stores, "realizing the potential business opportunity offered in Canandaigua for a progressive chain store" (in the words of that day's issue of the Daily Messenger), announced the store's impending opening on April 29, 1942; it closed eight years later. After Acme's closure, the building was subdivided and served as headquarters for a revolving door of small local businesses; it's vacant now, but under renovation (hence the uncovering of the sign), and thankfully, a petition by preservation-minded citizens was enough to convince Canandaigua's City Planning Commission to reverse their earlier decision that the sign should be removed or covered.

images.filename: South Main Street, Canandaigua, New York - 20210610.jpg
images.caption: Looking southward along South Main Street (New York State Routes 21 and 332) in historic downtown Canandaigua, New York on a beautiful June 2021 evening. These buildings form the core of the Canandaigua Historic District, established in 1984 and expanded in 2016 to include these further-north blocks of Main Street.
